text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria has agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on most issues related to the implementation of a currency board designed to stabilise the country's crumbling economy, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said. @

Differences remain in the area of the bank stabilisation policies as the IMF recommends to make the banking system more sustainable under the currency board system but the cabinet said it prefers to stabilise the banks before the board is introduced.

-- Russia's Rosneft oil company officially announced it would bid for a majority stake in Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim. Rosneft officials said if its bid was rejected it would concentrate its activities in the Georgian Black Sea port of Tuapse instead and could flood Bulgaria, Macedonia and Serbia with cheaper fuel. @

-- Bulgaria hopes to receive part of the money from the sale of a 60 percent stake in Bulgaria's soda ash producer Sodi-Devnya to the Belgian chemical company Solvay SA even before the sale was finalised, Bulgarian deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.

-- Drinking water supply charges are expected to fall by about 20 percent if the interim cabinet approves an agreement between the Construction ministry and the National Electricity Company that state water supply companies paid lower prices for the energy they use. @
-- The Sofia airport posted 567.91 million levs net profit for 1996, an airport senior official said.
-- The state agricultural fund Zemedelie said it would extend 2.5 billion levs to producers to support the spring maize sowing.

-- Depositors in Bulgarian commercial banks lost 75.08 percent of the value of their savings due to the high inflation in the first two months of this year, central bank figures showed. High inflation erased 67.63 levs per each 100 levs deposited in the banks in February alone. @

-- Bulgaria's Association of commercial banks said its members agreed to set up minimum service charges at 50 percent over Bankservice interbank electronic settlement system charges due to high inflation and the lev fall since the beginning of the year. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
